Adjudicating the MAYBE tier

Source: vignettes/adjudicating-maybe.Rmd
adjudicating-maybe.Rmd

The tier this is about

A pfmatch run sorts every grant identity into three tiers. On BASELINE-2026-10C’s augmented arm, over 4,748 identities:

tier identities share what it means
YES 2979 62.74% accepted automatically
MAYBE 1044 21.99% candidates surfaced, none decisive
NO 725 15.27% nothing surfaced, or vetoed

The clear rate is YES over identities, 62.74%. YES+MAYBE is 84.73% and is not a clear rate: pf_status() returns MAYBE precisely because the cascade could not choose, and dev/ADJUDICATION-PLAN.md records two separate attempts to accept the tier automatically, both of which failed. The second measured 72% precision on 200 cases after the first had measured 100% on 18.

So the 22 points between 62.74% and 84.73% are recoverable only by review, and the question is what kind of reviewer is worth paying for.

What a reviewer is given

pf_adjudicate() builds the packet: up to five candidate EINs per grant with BMF name, address, NTEE code and definition, activity text, subsection, assets and revenue, plus the filed grant and the filing foundation’s own sector. On top of that, for every candidate and not just the top pick, the NTEEv2 description and the Form 990 Part III mission and program text — which on 56 otherwise-unresolvable cases decided 45.

Two fields in that packet carry more weight than their size suggests.

cand_name is not the whole name. The BMF’s own display name differs from the matched name on 29% of candidate rows, and where it differs it often settles the case: two candidates both matched as “Wake Forest University” are in fact Mortar Board and Psi Chi The International Honor Society in Psychology. Omit it and the case reads as an unresolvable same-name tie.

NONE has to be a first-class answer. In the labelled sets, roughly a quarter of cases have no correct candidate in the packet at all. A reviewer that cannot decline will manufacture exactly that many false positives, and a scoring scheme that assumes an answer exists will not notice.

Three strategies

Each adjudicates the same frozen packet. They differ in the model and in whether the reviewer may leave the packet and search the web.

light — Haiku 5.5, packet only, one request per case, structured JSON out. This is the only tier that is obviously affordable at a million cases.

deep — Opus 5.5 at high effort, still packet only. Same text, same instructions, bigger model.

deep + search — Opus 5.5 with the server-side web search tool, instructed to establish who the filed recipient actually is before deciding, and to record what it found. This is the only configuration that can discover the right answer is absent rather than merely unproven.

cascade — light everywhere, escalating only the cases light itself flags low-confidence (14–16% of the tier) to one of the deep tiers.

Clearance, quality, and cost

Clearance is measured on 68 MAYBEs drawn simple-random and post-stratified on the tier’s tie rate. Precision and accuracy are measured on 200 cases with hand-adjudicated answers. Cost is token cost per case with cache traffic included, expressed as a ratio with light set to 1.

strategy model web clears precision on what it clears overall accuracy cost (light = 1)
light Haiku 5.5 no 57.8% 100.0% 82.5% 1
deep Opus 5.5 no 74.2% 99.3% 94.5% 44
deep + search Opus 5.5 yes 70.7% 97.1% 90.5% 102
cascade to deep Haiku then Opus no 67.2% 99.3% 90.0% 7
cascade to deep + search Haiku then Opus yes 64.8% 97.8% 89.0% 15

Precision is the share of an arm’s own MATCH verdicts that name the right EIN. Accuracy is the share of all its verdicts that are right, including its declines. The two differ because an arm can be cautious: light commits to only 59% of cases and is right on every one of them.

Three things to read out of that table.

Precision is not the problem. Every tier is at or near 100% on what it commits to — 118 of 118 for light, 143 of 144 for deep. These reviewers do not invent matches. They differ almost entirely in how much they are willing to clear, which makes clearance, not precision, the lever.

light is extraordinary value. At 1/44th the cost of deep it clears 57.8% of the tier with perfect precision on this sample. It is not as good — its overall accuracy is 82.5% against 94.5% — but its errors are declines, not false matches.

deep + search is dominated. It clears less than deep (70.7% vs 74.2%), is less precise (97.1% vs 99.3%), is less accurate (90.5% vs 94.5%), and costs 2.3 times more. There is no column in which it wins.

Where that leaves the match rate

The honest figure is YES + (MAYBE × clearance × precision) — a MAYBE cleared to the wrong EIN is not a match, it is a silent error that is never reviewed again.

adjudication strategy MAYBEs won overall match rate cost (light = 1)
none (the cascade alone) – 62.74% 0
light 603 75.44% 1
deep 770 78.95% 44
deep + search 717 77.84% 102
cascade to deep 696 77.41% 7
ceiling (YES + MAYBE) 1,044 84.73% –

So adjudication moves the match rate from 62.74% to between 75% and 79%, and the choice of tier is worth about 3.5 points while the choice of whether to adjudicate at all is worth 12 to 16.

The cost-quality frontier has three points on it and two of them are not obvious:

  • light, at cost 1, buys 12.7 of those points.
  • cascade to deep, at cost 7, buys 14.7.
  • deep everywhere, at cost 44, buys 16.2.

deep + search and cascade to deep + search are both off the frontier — strictly worse and strictly dearer. Whether the last 1.5 points are worth going from cost 7 to cost 44 depends on what an uncleared MAYBE costs downstream, which is a judgement this vignette cannot make for you.

Why confidence is the thing to route on

Each tier reports its own confidence. On the 200 labelled cases that self-report separates right answers from wrong ones very sharply (Fisher exact, high+medium vs low, p < 0.00001):

stated confidence light deep deep + search
high 98/98 = 100.0% 136/136 = 100.0% 162/166 = 97.6%
medium 60/74 = 81.1% 47/54 = 87.0% 18/28 = 64.3%
low 7/28 = 25.0% 6/10 = 60.0% 1/6 = 16.7%

A high-confidence verdict from light or deep was right on every one of 98 and 136 cases respectively. That is what makes the cascade work: the cheap tier knows which of its answers not to trust, so escalation can be targeted at the 14% it flags rather than sprayed across the tier.

It also means the cheap tier’s failures announce themselves, which is exactly what the geographic auto-accept rule could not do — that rule was 72% precise and silent about which 28%.

By evidence class, light’s weak spot is INFER: 65.5% correct, against 95.4% for QUOTE and 100% for NTEE. Reasoning over the whole packet without a quotable fact is where it goes wrong, and INFER plus low confidence is a better escalation trigger than either alone.

The search result, and what it actually means

Search was expected to be the most valuable tier. It is not, and the ablation — Opus at the same effort on the identical packet with search removed — says so on 227 paired cases (exact McNemar on discordant pairs):

comparison discordant pairs gained / lost p reading
model: light to deep 32 29 / 3 < 0.0001 deep is better
search: deep to deep + search 9 1 / 8 0.039 search is WORSE
total: light to deep + search 35 27 / 8 0.0019 deep + search is better

The model effect is large and certain. The search effect is significant in the wrong direction: search fixed 0 cases and broke 8.

That finding needs its mechanism stated, because “search makes it worse” is not quite what happened. Every one of the eight is search holding a stricter standard of entity identity than the human labellers did:

  • ERLANGER LIONS CLUB — search found the club’s own EIN (61-6034245), saw it was not among the candidates, and answered NONE. The label accepts the candidate as correct.
  • HABITAT FOR HUMANITY NEW YORK CITY AND WESTCHESTER COUNTY — search found the filed name is exactly the legal name of a different EIN, and declined.
  • BUNKER HILL COMMUNITY COLLEGE — search noted the candidate is the college’s separate foundation, not the college, and declined.

In each, search is arguably more right than the label. The labels encode “the best available BMF row”; search applies “the exact legal entity”. Those are different conventions, and this project has never written down which one it means — dev/ADJUDICATION-PLAN.md flags the entity-versus-fundraising-arm question as unsettled policy and that is precisely what is biting here.

So the defensible conclusion is narrower than the p-value: against the convention these labels encode, search costs accuracy and money. Settle the convention before concluding search is useless.

One thing search does that nothing else can: it establishes that an answer is absent. 39 of its verdicts came back CONTRADICTED — it found the organisation and showed its EIN is not among the candidates. A packet-only NONE means “I cannot tell”; a searched NONE means “I checked”. The first needs a human, the second can be closed. That is worth keeping for the residue even if it is wrong for the bulk.

Search also makes the model surer without making it righter: it puts 83% of verdicts at high confidence against deep’s 68%, while scoring lower. Rising confidence with falling accuracy is the one pattern that should worry anyone routing on confidence.

What none of this establishes

  • Precision over the YES mass is still unmeasured. Every ground-truth label this project holds came from a cell the pipeline itself produced, so nothing here speaks to the 62.74% that was never in doubt.
  • The accuracy figures are not tier-level. They come from three separately-drawn label sets, one deliberately subsampled. Accuracy is reported within stratum in dev/ADJ-CAL-RESULTS.log for that reason, and the only unbiased clearance estimate is the 68-case random draw.
  • One run is one draw. temperature cannot be set on this API version, so determinism is not available; run-to-run variance is measured by repeating a stage, not assumed away.
  • The packet shows five candidates. On 7 of 100 cases the close band held more than five — 41, in one case — so a NONE can mean “not in the five” rather than “not in the BMF”.
  • Cost ratios are token costs. Web search is billed per use on top, at about 2 searches per case, so the deep + search ratio of 102 understates it.

Reproducing

dev/ADJUDICATION-EXPERIMENT.md is the design note. The stages are dev/adjudicate-*.R: a preflight, the packet builders, the three arms, and the two scoring passes. They need ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; the packets are frozen to disk so the arms and the scoring can be re-run without touching the matcher.
